prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 物流运费与时效表 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 5 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "华东地区" spans 1 col × 2 row; "华南地区" spans 1 col × 2 row; "新疆、西藏全境及内蒙古阿拉善盟、青海玉树等区域，" spans 4 col × 1 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "目的地区域" · longest unbreakable word 14px · one-line width 67px
  col 2: header "省份" · longest unbreakable word 14px · one-line width 27px
  col 3: header "首重（元）" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 67px
  col 4: header "续重（元/kg）" · longest unbreakable word 60px · one-line width 86px
  col 5: header "时效" · longest unbreakable word 27px · one-line width 253px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 480px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 479px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r1B: widths [88, 48, 75, 107, 160] · table 479×387px · row heights [53, 33, 53, 33, 53, 33, 53, 73] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [88, 48, 88, 81, 173] · table 479×347px · row heights [53, 33, 53, 33, 33, 33, 33, 73] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2A: widths [88, 48, 75, 88, 180] · table 480×347px · row heights [53, 33, 53, 33, 33, 33, 33, 73] · column headers wrapped 2/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [88, 48, 68, 81, 194] · table 480×347px · row heights [53, 33, 53, 33, 33, 33, 33, 73] · column headers wrapped 2/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [75, 48, 88, 81, 187] · table 480×347px · row heights [53, 33, 53, 33, 33, 33, 33, 73] · column headers wrapped 2/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3A: widths [88, 48, 75, 83, 185] · table 480×347px · row heights [53, 33, 53, 33, 33, 33, 33, 73] · column headers wrapped 2/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3B: widths [88, 48, 68, 83, 192] · table 480×347px · row heights [53, 33, 53, 33, 33, 33, 33, 73] · column headers wrapped 2/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3C: widths [88, 48, 88, 83, 172] · table 480×347px · row heights [53, 33, 53, 33, 33, 33, 33, 73] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}

log.raw: {"preferred":["r1C"],"acceptable":["r3C","r2A","r3A"],"bad":[{"design":"r2B","why":"省份 列 68px 装两字省名（实需 48px），留下约 20px 死白，同时把 首重/续重 两个表头都逼到折行；多出的宽度给了最不需要它的列。"},{"design":"r3B","why":"同 r2B：省份列虚胖 20px，而 续重 列拿到 83px 仍低于 107px 的单行阈值，宽度白给、表头照旧折行，属双重浪费。"},{"design":"r2C","why":"为把 时效 抬到 187px，把行锚点列压到 75px，导致表头 目的地区域 断成“目的地区/域”，语义断在词中间；正文 华东地区 也贴边，整表最关键的定位列失去分量。"},{"design":"r1B","why":"把 续重 抬到 107px 换来单行表头，但代价是 时效 只剩 160px：4 行正文折成两行，表高 387px（比同表头折行数的 r1C 高 40px），行高 53/33 交替，纵向节奏破碎——用最长的阅读列去换一个本可干净折行的表头，优先级错置。"}],"contrast":{"widths":[96,96,96,96,95],"why":"看似“整齐均分”，实则无视内容：省份只需 48px 却占 96px，时效 只剩 95px，几乎所有时效单元格折成三行，表高暴涨、扫读节奏全毁。"},"ranges":[[88,96],[48,54],[88,94],[78,96],[165,180]],"rationale":"时效列承载全表最长文本（偏远地区合并说明一行 253px，另有多个双行单元格），应吸收几乎全部余量；省份列只需 48px，多给就是死白。所有候选都落在同一条前沿上：要么花 107px 让 续重（元/kg） 单行，把 时效 压到 ≤172px 使正文多折行、表高增到 387px；要么让该表头干净地断成“续重 / （元/kg）”，把表高锁在 347px。r1C 选了后者，同时保住 目的地区域 与 首重（元） 不折行，全表只有 1 个表头折行、正文行高统一 33px。r2C 的折行落在“目的地区/域”这种词中断裂上，代价与收益完全不对等，因此最差。","principles":{"general":["表头折行若断在语义边界（首重/（元）、续重/（元/kg））几乎无损；断在词中间（目的地区/域）则破坏行锚点的可识别性，代价远高。","宽度分配应看“文本量×换行代价”，而不是列数或对称：承载长句的列拿余量，短标识列压到阈值即可。","判断优劣要先看行高序列：行高忽高忽低说明某列宽度已越过折行阈值，是宽度错配的直接证据。","当某个折行阈值（此处 107px）会挤占更重要的列时，宁可让表头折行，也别为了‘表头全单行’牺牲正文。","省/地区这类 2–4 字的短列一旦明显宽于其最长词，会形成视觉空洞，破坏列间的节奏感。"],"specific":["本表列宽下限由内容精确给出：目的地区域 88、省份 48、首重（元） 88、续重（元/kg） 107、时效 48；479px 总和装不下全部单行表头（需 379 + 时效），因此必须接受至少一个表头折行。","偏远地区说明跨 4 列合并，其折行由第 2–5 列总宽决定，所以压窄省份列反而改善长说明的排版。","时效列在 173px 左右已达最优（表高 347px）；降到 160px 立即多出两行 53px 的行高，160 是硬性下限。"]},"tradeoffs":"有人会坚持所有表头单行、把 时效 压到 148px 以内，认为表头整齐优先于正文高度；也有人（如 r2A）愿意让两个表头干净折行以换取 时效 180px 的宽松。r1C 与 r3C 只差 1–2px 的分配，可视为同一设计。","uncertain":"r3C 与 r1C 在实际渲染中几乎不可分辨，是否应并列为 preferred 存在分歧；此外偏远地区这条合并说明是否应改为独占整行的脚注式排版（从而不再受列宽约束），是超出“只调列宽”范围但值得讨论的方向。"}
